# Archive Handbook (synthetic fixture)

## Labels

Every archive box carries a label on its short side so it can be read when the box sits on a shelf. A label must contain the collection code, the box number within the collection, the date range of the records inside and the retention category. Labels are printed, never handwritten, because handwriting fades and is misread during retrieval. The collection code always comes first because shelves are ordered by collection; the box number follows so staff can find the exact box without opening its neighbours. The date range tells a reader at a glance whether the box can hold the record they need, which saves pulling boxes that cannot contain it. The retention category decides when the box is reviewed for disposal, so a missing category means the box is never reviewed and space is wasted. Replace a damaged label the same day; a box without a readable label is moved to the intake shelf until it is relabelled.

## Retention

Retention categories are short, standard and permanent. Short records are reviewed after two years, standard records after seven years and permanent records are never destroyed. When a review date arrives, staff compare the box against the retention schedule, record the decision in the disposal log and either destroy the box securely or extend its review by one category period. A box is never destroyed without a logged decision, and permanent boxes are reviewed only for their condition, not for disposal. Mixing categories in one box is not allowed because the whole box would have to follow the longest period, which defeats the purpose of shorter categories.
